Content production policy regarding phimosis treatment on this site

Medical procedures such as medical diets, double plastic surgery, and phimosis surgery are important topics that are closely related to each individual's health condition, constitution, cost, and schedule.

In particular, regarding phimosis surgery, the necessity and options for treatment vary depending on the condition, such as pseudophimosis, true phimosis, and cantonal phimosis.

Difference between insurance medical treatment and free medical treatment

Whether public medical insurance covers phimosis surgery depends on your symptoms, the need for treatment, and the medical institution you visit.

  • Insurance medical treatment:True phimosis or cantonal phimosis may require medical treatment and may meet the requirements for insurance coverage.
  • Free medical treatment:As a general rule, the entire cost of cosmetic procedures or treatments that do not meet the requirements for insurance coverage must be paid by the patient.

*Prior confirmation is required as treatment for the same symptoms differs depending on the treatment content and medical institution.

Physical risks associated with surgery

Because phimosis surgery involves a surgical procedure, the following symptoms and complications may occur after surgery.

  • Bleeding, pain, swelling, internal bleeding
  • Inflammation such as infection or suppuration
  • Changes in skin tightness or sensation
  • Scars, scars, keloids, etc.

There are individual differences in the severity of symptoms and the postoperative course, and you may not be able to achieve the desired result. When undergoing a treatment, be sure to have your doctor explain not only the treatment method, but also the possible risks and postoperative measures, and make a decision after fully understanding the procedure.

Regarding consultations for those under 18 years of age

For medical examinations or surgeries for minors, written consent from a parent or guardian or accompanying person may be required according to clinic regulations. Age-based conditions and required documents vary by medical institution, so please check before making a reservation.
